Hand-line fishing — the story in four pictures

Before you step into the boat, here is how it goes — the way it has always been done from this shore. No rod: just line, hook and bait, and knowing the water.

You can open this storyboard again any time from the map key.

Bula! Welcome to the fishing boat.

The storyboard showed you the fishing in four pictures. Now drag to look around, and walk with the arrow pad — hold ▲ ▼ ◀ ▶ to move (on a keyboard, hold W A S D or the arrow keys) between the shore and the boat. Tap a numbered marker — or tap an item in the scene — to learn what it is. A little map in the corner, drawn on bark cloth, shows the places and where you are; its key is the index to the scene, the story and the storyboard. Ika (fish), Wai (water), Manu (bird) and Vale (house) are checked Fijian words; the thatched house is labelled Bure / Vale — “bure” is the founder-supplied name for it, still to be checked by Taniela. Every other word is added only after checking by fluent speakers, so those labels stay in English for now. On the shore behind the boat you’ll see a real village mix — the bure alongside a small corrugated iron house, breadfruit trees, and a woven mat on the sand.
